text:
sophia: heads up — private deploy (eu-west1) flagged unusual KMS Decrypt calls from svcacc `redwood-runner` at ~05:12 UTC. high rate for ~3 mins. can someone triage? :eyes:
raj: pinging infra logs + splunk link — can you paste the raw entries?
sophia: pasted snippet from splunk: `2026-03-15T05:12:22Z KMSDecrypt key=projects/priv-kms/keys/rlw-01 caller=svcacc:redwood-runner@proj`
raj: that caller shouldn't directly call KMS. which pod/service account?
devon: quick lookup -> `kubectl get pods -n redwood -o wide | grep runner` shows `runner-5c9b7  1/1  Running  10.10.45.21`
devon: check SA binding: `kubectl get rolebinding -n redwood | grep runner` -> `runner-binding   role/infra-runner -> sa:redwood:runner`
maria: who granted `infra-runner` the KMS decrypt permission? cluster role?
devon: found clusterrolebinding: `infra-ops-crb` bound to `system:serviceaccount:redwood:runner` and group `ci-runners`. output: 
```
NAME               ROLE
infra-ops-crb      roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
```
ops-oncall: incident-bot detected anomalous KMS traffic and auto-created a mitigation task. recommend immediate isolation: deny egress for namespace redwood until we confirm.
raj: agreed. steps I propose: 1) revoke SA tokens for runner, 2) remove infra-ops-crb binding, 3) apply temporary netpol denying egress except to known telemetry, 4) rotate KMS key if suspicious, 5) enable enhanced audit logging for KMS.
sophia: starting step 1 and 2 now.
devon: helper commands: 
```
# revoke tokens
kubectl delete secret $(kubectl get sa runner -n redwood -o jsonpath='{.secrets[0].name}') -n redwood
# remove binding
kubectl delete clusterrolebinding infra-ops-crb
```
maria: while you do that, I'm drafting a minimal NetworkPolicy to block egress from the namespace to the internet and only allow to KMS proxy and metrics collector.
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: redwood-temporary-egress-lockdown
  namespace: redwood
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.20.30.0/24   # kms proxy cluster IPs
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
devon: note: for private deployments, DNS leakage can bypass ipBlocks if kube-dns resolves external. prefer to point to internal proxy IPs.
ops-oncall: applying netpol now.
ops-oncall: `kubectl apply -f tmp-netpol.yaml` -> STATUS: applied.
ops-oncall: monitoring: egress attempts to KMS from runner dropped (403) within 20s. KMS decrypt rate back to baseline.
raj: please capture audit lines (KMS + kube-apiserver). we need a clear timeline for postmortem.
incident-bot: ticket created INC-2026-1734 by ops-oncall — severity: medium. follow-up meeting scheduled in 45m.
sophia: short root cause notes: unauthorized clusterrolebinding created by a CI job (infra/packer-runner) that used a service account with overly broad privileges. we need RBAC guardrails on CI to prevent `clusterrolebinding` creation.
maria: action items: 1) add OPA Gate to block CRB and CR creation from CI pipelines, 2) audit existing clusterrolebindings for unexpected SAs, 3) add alert on KMS decrypt spike for private deployments, 4) update playbook to include netpol fallback.
devon: I'll open PR for netpol + a templated egress-lockdown for Private deployments. link in thread when ready.
raj: I'll harden KMS key policy to require specific service account identity and rotate keys if we see any suspect use.
ops-oncall: mitigation confirmed. setting incident state -> mitigated. Please attach logs to INC-2026-1734.
sophia: thanks all. postmortem owners: devon (network), raj (kms + audit), maria (rbac + ci), sophia (owner). :thumbsup:
ops-oncall: leaving a short runbook note: when KMS spike -> revoke SA, apply egress netpol, gather KMS audit, check CRB history, escalate to sec.
incident-bot: summary appended to ticket: "temporary netpol lockdown stopped unauthorized decrypts; CRB created by CI job; RBAC pipeline guards required."
raj: one follow-up question — do we want to add egress default-deny to all Private clusters as standard? sounds disruptive but increases isolation.
maria: yes, propose a gradual rollout: start with dev clusters + canary, whitelist internal infra proxies. then full private clusters after a week of monitoring.
sophia: agreed. I'll add that to roadmap/epic and loop in solutions/security. closing thread for now.
